name: Nintendo Switch
whySpecs: The original Nintendo Switch is limited to the UHS-I interface with a maximum speed of 104MB/s. UHS-II and SD Express cards are backward compatible and will work, but they downclock to the console's UHS-I speed, so their extra performance is wasted money. The console uses standard microSD/microSDHC/microSDXC cards. V30 rated cards from trusted brands provide the best reliability for downloading large digital libraries. All Nintendo-branded SanDisk microSD cards (Zelda, Pokémon, Mario, etc.) are standard UHS-I format and work perfectly on the original Switch. 2TB microSDXC cards from brands like SanDisk and Silicon Power are commercially available and have been verified to work.

faq.q: Does the Switch support cards larger than 1TB?
faq.a: Yes. 2TB microSDXC cards from SanDisk and other brands work after a Switch system update.

faq.q: Can I use my phone's microSD card in the Switch?
faq.a: Yes. Back up the phone data first: the Switch formats the card and erases it.

faq.q: Do I need a V30 card for the Switch?
faq.a: No. V30 is a video rating. Any U1 or U3 card from a known brand loads games at the console's full speed.

notes: Limited to UHS-I speeds (~104MB/s maximum). V30 is recommended for reliability. Compatible with all officially licensed Nintendo-branded SanDisk microSD cards (Zelda, Pokémon, Mario, Yoshi, Animal Crossing, Fortnite).
metaDescription: The Nintendo Switch tops out at UHS-I speed (104MB/s). UHS-II and SD Express cards work but downclock to UHS-I, so their extra speed is wasted money.

name: Nintendo Switch OLED
whySpecs: The Switch OLED has 64GB of internal storage, double the original model. Like every original Switch, its slot is UHS-I (about 100 MB/s). UHS-II and SD Express cards fit but run at UHS-I speed, so they cost more for nothing.

faq.q: Should I buy a UHS-II card for the Switch OLED?
faq.a: No. The slot is UHS-I, so a UHS-II card loads games no faster.

faq.q: Can I use my original Switch's card in the OLED?
faq.a: Yes. All original Switch models use the same card format.

faq.q: What size microSD card should I get for the Switch OLED?
faq.a: 512GB or 1TB if you buy digital. Many recent games take 10GB to 30GB each.

notes: OLED users typically purchase larger cards due to increased digital game library usage. UHS-I only (~104MB/s), despite higher internal storage.
metaDescription: The Switch OLED has a UHS-I microSD slot, like every original Switch. UHS-II and Express cards fit but load no faster. Buy 512GB or 1TB for digital games.

name: Steam Deck
whySpecs: The Steam Deck's microSD slot is UHS-I, so cards top out around 100 MB/s no matter what the label says. Games load from the card in small random reads, which is what the A1 and A2 app ratings measure. 2TB cards such as the SanDisk Extreme and Lexar Play work. microSD prices rose across all capacities in 2026 because of a NAND flash shortage.

faq.q: Can I use fast V60 cards?
faq.a: Yes, but they won't load games any faster. The Steam Deck's UHS-I slot caps reads near 100 MB/s, so a V60 or UHS-II card performs like a good V30 A2 card.

faq.q: What is the max SD card size for Steam Deck?
faq.a: 2TB, the microSDXC limit. 2TB cards from SanDisk and Lexar work in both the LCD and OLED models.

faq.q: Does the Steam Deck OLED use a different microSD card?
faq.a: No. The OLED model has the same UHS-I microSD slot as the LCD model, so the same cards work in both.

notes: Steam Deck uses UHS-I only. V30 cards sufficient. Recommend 256GB+ for game library.
metaDescription: Steam Deck takes UHS-I microSD cards up to 2TB. Buy an A2 card in 512GB or 1TB for your game library; V60 and UHS-II cards load no faster.

faq.q: Will a microSD Express card work in my original Switch or Switch OLED?
faq.a: Yes, at UHS-I speed. Express cards are backward compatible with UHS-I slots, so one card can move between consoles. Switch 2 games still need the Switch 2.

faq.q: What microSD card should I buy for Switch 2?

faq.q: Why is my R36S showing a black screen?
faq.a: This is almost always caused by a failed stock SD card. The unbranded cards included in the box are extremely low quality. Flash a fresh image of ArkOS onto a brand-name card (like SanDisk) to fix this immediately.

faq.q: Can I use a Samsung EVO card in the OS slot (TF1)?
faq.a: It depends on your device batch. Some R36S units have trouble booting from newer Samsung EVO cards in the TF1 slot. We recommend using a SanDisk Ultra card for the OS (TF1) to guarantee a successful boot, and using Samsung cards for the Game (TF2) slot.

faq.q: Should I use a Single Card or Dual Card setup?
faq.a: A Dual Card setup is highly recommended. By keeping your OS on a small card (16-32GB) and your games on a large card (128GB+), you can update or re-flash the ArkOS firmware without ever deleting your game library or save files.

faq.q: Do I need to copy files from the old card?
faq.a: Yes, specifically the '.dtb' files. Before throwing away the stock card, copy the `.dtb` files from the BOOT partition. You may need these to make your screen work correctly with new firmware versions (Panel 4/Panel 5 screens).

notes: The best value budget handheld of 2024/2025, but requires technical setup. SEO Tip: Users often search for 'R36S ArkOS Guide'—having the right SD card is step 1.
